newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Two foreign firms sign Tanzania gold mining deal.
newsitem.headline: Two foreign firms sign Tanzania gold mining deal.

text.p: Two foreign mining firms have signed a $50 million joint venture to start gold mining in northern Tanzania, the government said in a statement on Thursday.
The project was the first large-scale gold mining operation in the east African country, the government said.
Australian-based Resolute Ltd and British miner Samax Resources Ltd signed a 14-month mine development programme with production scheduled to start in mid-1998.
The deal was signed in the inland town of Dodoma on Wednesday by the Minister for Energy and Minerals, Abdallah Kigoda.

"When fully operational, the project is planned to produce 170,000 ounces (5.28 tonnes) of gold per annum from a conventional carbon-in-leach gold processing facility, treating two million ounces of gold-bearing ore each year," the statement said.
Estimates of the ore resource base at the Lusu mine site in northern Tabora region is 20 million tonnes containing 2.4 million ounces (74.6 tonnes). Projected mine life is 10 years.
The joint-venture partners say they are optimistic about new gold discoveries in the prospect covering 3,700 sq km.
A detailed geological investigation is currently being undertaken at a cost of $1.5 million over the next 12 months to assess additional ore bodies.
The main project costs were listed as a mineral processing plant, mine equipment, electrical, water and road services, mine design and construction and staff housing.
According to the ministry, the project will be a major economic boost to the region and the Tanzanian economy which will earn $3 million in direct taxes and royalties.
The people of Nzega district will benefit from an upgrading of their water supply, electricity improvements, new roads and other social amenities.
The project will also employ 300 Tanzanians in temporary jobs during the construction phase and 250 permanent jobs when the mine becomes operational.
In the June 19 budget, finance minister Daniel Yona promised mining companies total exemption of all taxes on importation of machinery and equipment until the first year of production.
Machinery and equipment imported after the first year of production would be subjected to a low rate of five percent sales tax and import duties.
As a further incentive, he announced export and stamp duty on mineral exports would be abolished and 100 percent depreciation allowed on capital expenditure.
Withholding tax on dividends and profit-sharing tax for non-residents was set at 10 percent.

The government has identified the mining industry as a major economic prospect for mineral-rich Tanzania whose gold mining industry to date has been dominated by an estimated 500,000 small scale artisanal miners.
Accurate figures on Tanzania's gold production are difficult to obtain because of widespread smuggling of the metal, ministry sources said.
